student.headline: Keep the bench dry and orderly, use only the approved supply, and stop before changing a circuit.
hazards: Electric shock or burns from damaged equipment, exposed conductors or an unsuitable supply.
Short circuits and incorrect polarity can overheat wires, components or batteries and start a fire.
Hot tools, sharp wire ends, loose leads and crowded benches can cause burns, cuts and trips.
beforeStart: Complete the electrical workshop induction and locate the isolator, emergency stop, fire equipment, first aid and exits.
Get teacher permission for the exact circuit and use only the approved current-limited extra-low-voltage supply unless the task is specifically restricted and controlled.
Check leads, plugs, tools, guards and insulation; keep liquids away and remove metal jewellery.
dos: Switch off and confirm the circuit is de-energised before building, changing or inspecting connections.
Use insulated, correctly rated tools and test equipment as demonstrated.
Keep leads short and tidy, protect bare conductors, and report every fault or near miss.
donts: Do not work on mains wiring, switchboards, fixed installations or exposed live parts.
Do not bypass a fuse, RCD, guard, interlock, earth or current limit.
Do not use damaged equipment, wet hands, drinks, improvised adapters or overloaded outlets.
stop: A lead, plug, enclosure, tool or test instrument is damaged, hot, wet or modified.
There is a spark, shock, smell, smoke, unexpected reading or repeated protection trip.
You are unsure of the voltage, circuit state, polarity, rating or teacher instruction.

teacher.overview: Baseline controls for entry, conduct and supervised learning in the Electrical Trades workshop. It favours current-limited extra-low-voltage activities and does not authorise prescribed electrical work.
hazards: Electric shock or burns from damaged equipment, exposed conductors or an unsuitable supply.
Short circuits and incorrect polarity can overheat wires, components or batteries and start a fire.
Hot tools, sharp wire ends, loose leads and crowded benches can cause burns, cuts and trips.
riskAssessment: Apply the hierarchy of controls and keep student work within the demonstrated, assessed task boundary.
Electrical energy, stored energy, heat, chemicals and unexpected energisation must be considered together.
preStart: Define the permitted voltage/energy envelope and isolate mains training equipment from general student access.
Verify protective devices, emergency isolation, ventilation, housekeeping and dry conditions.
safeUse: Prefer battery or current-limited ELV systems where learning outcomes allow.
Control energisation through the teacher and use fault-finding methods appropriate to the assessed circuit.
Keep mains, EV high-voltage and other restricted systems outside the general student task boundary.
shutdown: De-energise supplies, disconnect batteries where specified, discharge stored energy by the approved method, and leave controls at zero/off.
Account for tools and components, clean the bench, and quarantine faults.
restrictions: This SOP does not authorise prescribed electrical work, live work, switchboard access, mains construction or repair, EV/HEV high-voltage work, or work on unknown equipment.
disposal: Segregate electronic, battery, chemical and general waste under the school waste plan; do not place hazardous waste in ordinary bins or drains.
storage: Store equipment isolated, dry and protected from damage; secure restricted tools, components and substances from unauthorised access.
furtherInformation: Review the local RAMS whenever the equipment, circuit, product, room or learner group changes.
firstAid: Stop work and alert the teacher. Isolate the supply only when it is safe to do so; do not touch a person who may still be in contact with electricity.
Call emergency services for electric shock, burns, fire, breathing difficulty, collapse or significant chemical exposure, and follow the PHS first-aid procedure.
teacherChecks: Confirm the exact task is permitted, the equipment and controls are suitable, and the learner has been instructed and assessed.
Remove damaged, modified, wet, overheated or uncertain equipment from service and label/report it.

student.headline: Identify every energy source, isolate it, prevent reconnection and prove the approved training circuit is de-energised.
hazards: A circuit can remain energised through the wrong isolator, backfeed, battery, capacitor or another supply.
Someone can restore power while work is in progress.
An unsuitable or unverified tester can give a false “dead” result.
beforeStart: Use this process only on the teacher-approved training system and follow the demonstrated isolation plan.
Identify all sources, including batteries, capacitors, generators, UPS units and mechanical stored energy.
Obtain the specified lock/tag and approved test instrument.
dos: Switch off loads, isolate every source, lock/tag where provided and control the key as directed.
Prove the tester on a known source, test the required points, then re-prove the tester.
Treat the circuit as energised until the teacher confirms the isolation and stored energy is controlled.
donts: Do not perform isolation on a mains installation, switchboard or equipment outside the approved training task.
Do not rely on a switch position, indicator lamp, software command or someone else’s word.
Do not remove another person’s lock/tag or reconnect a supply without the teacher’s release process.
stop: The diagram, source, isolator, lock point or test point does not match the plan.
The tester fails its proving check or any reading is unexpected.
A second source, damaged conductor or uncontrolled stored energy is found.

teacher.overview: A supervised isolation workflow for approved training systems. It teaches source identification, prevention of reconnection and verified de-energisation without authorising work on mains installations.

Control stored electrical and non-electrical energy before contact.
Only the authorised person may release the isolation after the work area has been checked.
shutdown: Confirm guards/covers are restored, tools and people are clear, and the circuit is safe before controlled re-energisation.
Record and quarantine any discrepancy or failed test instrument.
restrictions: Students must not isolate, test or work on mains installations or carry out prescribed electrical work under this general SOP.

student.headline: Select the right meter and range, inspect the leads, and connect only to the teacher-approved circuit.
hazards: Wrong terminals, range or function can short the circuit, damage the meter or expose the user to energy.
Damaged probes or leads can expose conductors.
A misleading reading can cause unsafe decisions.
beforeStart: Confirm the circuit is within the approved ELV/current-limited training range.
Check the meter, fuse, category/rating, probes, shrouds and insulation for the task.
Set the function, range and lead sockets before approaching the circuit.
dos: Hold probes behind the finger guards and keep exposed metal to a minimum.
De-energise before moving leads for current or resistance measurements unless the demonstrated method requires an energised ELV reading.
Compare the result with the expected range and stop on any mismatch.
donts: Do not use a multimeter on mains, switchboards, unknown supplies, EV/HEV high-voltage systems or exposed live parts.
Do not measure resistance/continuity on an energised circuit.
Do not change range, socket or connections carelessly while probes are in contact.
stop: The meter rating, circuit voltage or energy is unknown.
The display, fuse, lead or probe is damaged or the reading is unstable/unexpected.
A protection device operates, a component heats or the circuit behaves differently from the diagram.

teacher.overview: Selection and supervised use of electrical test instruments on approved training circuits. Measurement on higher-energy or prescribed systems is excluded.
hazards: Wrong terminals, range or function can short the circuit, damage the meter or expose the user to energy.
Damaged probes or leads can expose conductors.
A misleading reading can cause unsafe decisions.
riskAssessment: Apply the hierarchy of controls and keep student work within the demonstrated, assessed task boundary.
Electrical energy, stored energy, heat, chemicals and unexpected energisation must be considered together.
preStart: Match the instrument, probes, ratings and protection to the circuit; verify meter fuses and condition.
Set the permitted measurement methods and require teacher control of energisation.
safeUse: Use the lowest-energy practical source and test points designed for training.
Teach function/range/socket checks, probe placement and interpretation before independent handling.
For any prove-dead process, use the instrument and proving method required by the applicable procedure.
shutdown: Remove probes safely, switch off the circuit, return leads to the normal voltage/ohms sockets and store the meter protected.
restrictions: Students must not perform voltage testing on mains, switchboards, fixed wiring, unknown equipment or EV/HEV high-voltage systems.
disposal: Segregate electronic, battery, chemical and general waste under the school waste plan; do not place hazardous waste in ordinary bins or drains.

student.headline: Build with the supply off, check every connection, then energise the current-limited circuit with teacher permission.
hazards: Reversed polarity, wrong component values or wiring errors can overheat or rupture components.
Short circuits can heat wires, batteries and power supplies.
Sharp leads, hot components and loose wires can injure or create faults.
beforeStart: Confirm the schematic, maximum voltage/current and component ratings with the teacher.
Set the current-limited supply to zero/off and inspect the breadboard, leads and components.
Identify polarised parts and check capacitor, diode, LED and IC orientation.
dos: Build and alter connections only with power off.
Use colour-coded leads, trim/cover sharp ends, and keep wiring readable.
Ask the teacher to check the circuit before first energisation and after major changes.
donts: Do not connect the prototype directly to mains or an unapproved high-current battery.
Do not defeat current limiting or substitute a component with an unknown rating.
Do not touch or move a component that is hot, swollen, leaking or damaged.
stop: A component heats, swells, vents, smells, discolours or makes noise.
Current is higher or voltage lower than expected.
The circuit diagram, polarity or component rating is uncertain.

teacher.overview: Supervised construction and testing of current-limited ELV electronic circuits using breadboards or approved modules.
hazards: Reversed polarity, wrong component values or wiring errors can overheat or rupture components.

Sharp leads, hot components and loose wires can injure or create faults.
riskAssessment: Apply the hierarchy of controls and keep student work within the demonstrated, assessed task boundary.
Electrical energy, stored energy, heat, chemicals and unexpected energisation must be considered together.

safeUse: Require a power-off build/check stage before controlled energisation.
Use staged tests and current limits to contain wiring/component faults.
Maintain eye protection where components could fragment or vent.
shutdown: Switch off, allow hot parts to cool, discharge stored energy by the approved method and disconnect the source.
Remove failed components for investigation; do not return them to storage.
restrictions: No mains-derived exposed circuitry, improvised mains supplies, high-energy battery packs or pyrotechnic components.

student.headline: Use extraction at the joint, return the iron to its stand, and wash hands after handling solder.
hazards: The iron, molten solder and recently heated parts can cause burns or ignite materials.
Flux fumes can irritate or sensitise the airways; solder/residue can contaminate hands and surfaces.
Solder splashes, clipped leads and desoldering tools can injure eyes.
beforeStart: Use the approved temperature-controlled iron, stable stand and local extraction.
Check the cable, plug, tip, stand and extraction; clear paper, solvents and other combustibles.
Confirm the solder/flux product and any hygiene or RPE controls from the SDS and local assessment.
dos: Position extraction close enough to capture fume without cooling the joint excessively.
Hold work securely, keep hands clear and return the iron to the stand whenever it is not in use.
Wash hands after soldering and before eating; clean residues using only the approved method/product.
donts: Do not touch the tip, flick solder, leave the iron unattended or place it on the bench.
Do not eat, drink, touch your face or use an unknown solder/flux/cleaner.
Do not rely on a respirator instead of effective extraction; use RPE only when the assessed programme requires it.
stop: Extraction stops or fumes move into the breathing zone.
The iron, cable, stand or control is damaged or overheats.
Solder spits, a battery/component becomes hot, or you feel eye/airway irritation.

teacher.overview: Soldering and desoldering of electronic connections on approved low-voltage assemblies with heat, fume and contamination controls.
hazards: The iron, molten solder and recently heated parts can cause burns or ignite materials.
Flux fumes can irritate or sensitise the airways; solder/residue can contaminate hands and surfaces.
Solder splashes, clipped leads and desoldering tools can injure eyes.
riskAssessment: Apply the hierarchy of controls and keep student work within the demonstrated, assessed task boundary.
Electrical energy, stored energy, heat, chemicals and unexpected energisation must be considered together.
preStart: Review solder/flux/cleaner SDSs and assess fume capture at the actual bench.
Provide stable stands, temperature control, heat-resistant work surfaces, eye protection and hand-washing facilities.
safeUse: Capture flux fume at source and keep the operator out of the plume.

If RPE remains necessary after higher-order controls, select and manage it through a competent assessment in line with AS/NZS 1715 and use a product meeting AS/NZS 1716; fit testing, training, storage and facial-hair compatibility apply.
Treat lead-containing solder and residues as a hygiene/contamination issue; prefer approved lead-free processes where suitable.
shutdown: Return the iron to the stand, switch off/unplug as directed, allow it to cool and clean the bench without spreading residue.
restrictions: No soldering on energised equipment, batteries, mains assemblies or unknown circuits.
disposal: Segregate electronic, battery, chemical and general waste under the school waste plan; do not place hazardous waste in ordinary bins or drains.
storage: Store equipment isolated, dry and protected from damage; secure restricted tools, components and substances from unauthorised access.
furtherInformation: Review the local RAMS whenever the equipment, circuit, product, room or learner group changes.
firstAid: Stop work and alert the teacher. Isolate the supply only when it is safe to do so; do not touch a person who may still be in contact with electricity.

student.headline: Inspect before use, keep leads protected and dry, and treat every RCD trip as a fault to report.
hazards: Damaged plugs, sockets, leads or equipment can expose live parts or cause fire.
Leads can be crushed, cut, wet, overheated, coiled under load or create trip hazards.
An RCD reduces some shock risk but does not make unsafe equipment or behaviour safe.
beforeStart: Inspect the plug, pins, lead, socket, casing and strain relief before connecting.
Confirm the equipment is suitable for the environment and any required RCD protection is present.
Route the lead away from water, heat, sharp edges, doors, vehicles and walkways.
dos: Use only approved school equipment and operate the RCD test button at the interval/process set by the school.
Fully unwind extension reels when the load and manufacturer instructions require it.
Disconnect by holding the plug, and report/quarantine any defect or protection trip.
donts: Do not use taped, cut, crushed, burnt, loose, wet or exposed leads and plugs.
Do not daisy-chain boards, overload outlets, remove earth pins or use incompatible adapters.
Do not reset a tripped RCD or breaker repeatedly.
stop: An RCD/breaker trips, a plug or lead becomes hot, or there is arcing, smell or discolouration.
Equipment has been wet, dropped, crushed, modified or brought in without approval.
The lead cannot be routed without damage or a trip hazard.

student.headline: Do a pre-use visual check every time; a tag is not proof that equipment is safe today.
hazards: Damage can occur after a test/tag and may not be visible on a label.
An incorrect test method can expose the tester or damage equipment.
A passed tag can create false confidence if pre-use checks are skipped.
beforeStart: Check the plug, pins, lead, strain relief, casing, controls and guards before use.
Confirm the equipment belongs to the school system and is within any recorded inspection/test interval.
Ask the teacher about missing, illegible or expired records.
dos: Report and quarantine damaged, wet, modified or suspect equipment.
Continue visual checks even when a tag is present.
Use only equipment approved for the task and environment.
donts: Do not perform electrical safety testing or tagging unless you are specifically trained, authorised and supervised for that process.
Do not open, repair or rewire equipment or copy/alter a test label.
Do not use equipment merely because it has a current-looking tag.
stop: A tag/record is missing or conflicts with the equipment identity.
Any conductor, insulation, enclosure, guard, plug or control is damaged.
The equipment trips protection, tingles, sparks, smells, overheats or behaves unexpectedly.

teacher.overview: Student pre-use visual checks plus teacher guidance on the role and limits of inspection, testing and tagging.
hazards: Damage can occur after a test/tag and may not be visible on a label.
An incorrect test method can expose the tester or damage equipment.
A passed tag can create false confidence if pre-use checks are skipped.
riskAssessment: Apply the hierarchy of controls and keep student work within the demonstrated, assessed task boundary.
Electrical energy, stored energy, heat, chemicals and unexpected energisation must be considered together.
preStart: Establish a risk-based maintenance system for the environment and equipment type.
Ensure testing is carried out by a person competent for the equipment and test method, with suitable calibrated equipment and records.
safeUse: Testing and tagging is one way of checking safety; it does not replace visual inspection, maintenance or removal after damage.

student.headline: De-energise first, use the right stripping/crimping tool, and inspect every extra-low-voltage termination.
hazards: Blades, wire ends and clipped conductors can cut or puncture skin and eyes.
Damaged strands, loose crimps or exposed copper can overheat or short circuit.
A cable may be mistaken for ELV or remain connected to another source.
beforeStart: Confirm the cable is disconnected from every source and is part of the approved ELV training task.
Select the correct strip length, terminal and tool/die for the conductor.
Inspect tools, insulation and conductor condition; secure the work.
dos: Cut away from the body, control offcuts and keep fingers outside the tool jaws.
Avoid nicking strands; make the demonstrated crimp/termination and perform the specified visual/pull check.
Protect the finished connection against exposed conductor, strain and wrong polarity.
donts: Do not prepare or terminate mains, fixed-installation, unknown, energised or EV/HEV high-voltage cable.
Do not use teeth, knives, side cutters or an incorrect crimp tool as a substitute for the specified stripper/die.
Do not hide a weak, loose or damaged termination under heat-shrink or tape.
stop: The cable identity, voltage, source or conductor size is uncertain.
Strands are nicked/cut, insulation is damaged, or the terminal/tool does not match.
The termination fails its inspection or pull check.

student.headline: Assume capacitors are charged until the approved discharge method and measurement prove otherwise.
hazards: A capacitor can retain charge after the supply is removed.
Wrong polarity, over-voltage or excessive ripple/current can heat, vent or rupture a component.
Shorting a charged capacitor directly can create an arc, damage and flying material.
beforeStart: Identify all capacitors and their ratings/polarity on the approved ELV training circuit.
Switch off and isolate all sources, then wait the specified time.
Use the teacher-approved discharge device and meter method.
dos: Keep eye protection on and maintain polarity and rating checks during assembly.
Discharge through the specified resistor/device, then measure and re-check before contact.
Treat removed or long-stored components as uncertain until inspected and controlled.
donts: Do not touch terminals or assume a capacitor is safe because the indicator is off.
Do not discharge by placing a screwdriver or bare conductor across terminals.
Do not use swollen, leaking, damaged, incorrectly rated or unknown capacitors.
stop: Voltage remains, returns after discharge or the measurement is unstable.
A capacitor is hot, swollen, leaking, hissing or fitted backwards.
The capacitance, voltage, energy or discharge method is unknown.

student.headline: Confirm chemistry and polarity, set a current limit, and keep metal objects away from battery terminals.
hazards: A short circuit can produce intense heat, burns, fire or molten metal.
Incorrect charging, damage or wrong polarity can cause venting, leakage, thermal runaway or rupture.
Battery electrolyte and fumes can injure eyes, skin or lungs.
beforeStart: Identify the battery chemistry, voltage, condition and approved charger/supply.
Remove jewellery and loose metal items; use insulated connections and cover unused terminals.
Set the bench supply voltage/current limit with output off and have the teacher check polarity.
dos: Make or change connections with the output off and prevent accidental shorting.
Use only the charger/profile specified for that battery chemistry and monitor the task.
Keep batteries upright, ventilated as required and away from heat, sparks and combustibles.
donts: Do not charge swollen, leaking, hot, damaged, frozen, unknown or non-rechargeable batteries.
Do not mix cell types/ages, reverse polarity, exceed ratings or bypass protection/current limiting.
Do not work on EV/HEV traction batteries, orange cables or vehicle high-voltage systems.
stop: A battery or lead becomes hot, swells, leaks, vents, smells, sparks or makes noise.
The supply current is unexpected or protection operates.
The chemistry, charger, polarity, voltage or battery condition is uncertain.

stop: A container is unlabelled, leaking, damaged or incompatible substances are present.

student.headline: REFERENCE ONLY — Students must not perform mains or prescribed electrical work unless the EWRB trainee and supervision requirements are formally in place.
hazards: Mains and higher-energy systems can cause fatal electric shock, arc burns, fire or explosion.
Incorrect isolation, testing, earthing, polarity or protection can leave equipment dangerously energised.
Prescribed electrical work is legally restricted and requires the appropriate authorisation and supervision.
beforeStart: Do not begin this work; use this page for hazard and legal-awareness only.
Ask the teacher which ELV simulation or disconnected demonstration is permitted.
Treat all mains wiring, switchboards, fixed installations and unknown equipment as out of bounds.
dos: Follow barriers, signs and teacher directions around restricted electrical areas.
Report exposed parts, damaged covers, unusual heat, smell, sound, tingling or protection trips immediately.
In an emergency, keep clear, raise the alarm and isolate only if trained and it is safe to do so.
donts: Do not operate, use, perform or carry out prescribed electrical work under this general student SOP.
Do not open switchboards, fixed wiring, mains equipment or protective devices.
Do not test for voltage, bypass isolation, reset protection repeatedly or touch a person still connected to electricity.
stop: A cover, barrier, earth or protective device is missing or damaged.
There is a shock/tingle, arc, smoke, fire, smell, heat or unexpected energisation.
The person’s licence/certificate, scope of work or supervision arrangement is not confirmed.
